punchline: Two riders carried the same news on the same night, and only the one who knew whose door to knock on is remembered.
thirty_sec: On the night the British marched, Paul Revere and William Dawes both rode out with the same message. Revere woke militia leaders town after town. Dawes's ride barely registered, and Waltham heard too late. Gladwell says Revere was a Connector and a Maven: he knew many people and gathered information. Dawes was an ordinary man.
